frontier_act_119.text: As a cosponsor of the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, I'm working with @JayObernolte to ensure our regulatory framework keeps pace with sophisticated frontier AI models while fostering American innovation. The bill takes a targeted approach by focusing oversight on the most advanced frontier AI model developers while allowing startups and smaller innovators to build new technologies instead of navigating unnecessary federal red tape.

deepseek.reason: The speaker self-identifies as a cosponsor and praises the FRONTIER Act's targeted oversight approach.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly names the bill and identifies the speaker as a cosponsor.

export_controls.text: AI is changing the world and the U.S. can't afford to fall behind China. Yesterday, in @housescience, I focused on how Congress can support innovation the right way with targeted export controls, funding the AI Action Plan, and the energy and computing infrastructure needed to keep America ahead.👇

export_controls.text: Earlier this Congress I led a letter with Congressman McCormick, also on the Science Committee with me, raising concerns about the Biden Administration's proposed AI Diffusion Rule at the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which we believe risk overbroad export controls that could slow U.S. innovation and push some of our allies toward non-U.S. suppliers.
export_controls.context: A lawmaker questions a witness during a congressional hearing on the Advancing America's AI Action Plan.

china_race_dynamics.text:
Cutting edge Frontier AI models are now showing the ability to do things their creators didn’t intend or anticipate.  The implications are serious and must be addressed.   

This week, I participated in a @housescience roundtable with AI industry leaders to take a deeper look at the recent OpenAI/Hugging Face incident and the lessons we need to learn from the rapid advancement of Frontier models. As Congress grapples with establishing proper AI oversight, we must strike the right balance that encourages American innovation while protecting the public. Doing so will be critical to ensuring the AI race isn’t won by authoritarian regimes whose disregard for our Western democratic values could be catastrophic through the abuse or reckless use of this transformational technology.

deepseek.reason: The speaker frames proper AI oversight as critical so the AI race is not won by authoritarian regimes.
deepseek.confidence_reason: China is not named, but the AI-race and authoritarian-regimes framing is close to the target.

astra.reason: The speaker advocates safe AI leadership against authoritarian regimes without identifying competition with China.
astra.confidence_reason: An AI race is explicit, but identifying China as its target would require an inference beyond the supplied evidence.

china_race_dynamics.text: Keeping America ahead in AI means protecting consumers without holding back innovation. I met with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce’s Chamber Technology Engagement Center to talk about AI, data privacy and keeping American innovators competitive. We must get this right to support American innovation and stay ahead of Communist China.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says the US must stay ahead of Communist China in AI.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly frames staying ahead of China as a goal, though it is brief.

The Great American AI Act builds on the bipartisan House AI Task Force and represents an important step toward greater transparency and accountability for advanced AI systems.
